metadata.note: Month two (June 2026, Weeks 5-9). Month-as-a-whole structure. First person (reviewer request). Executive summary at beat two (B01), per reviewer. No non-professor names. Synthetic visuals only.

beats.narration_text: Month two was a standing start on a new toolchain. In five weeks I went from an empty environment to animated physics scenes a professor approved and asked me to continue — with one genuine animation bug solved along the way.

beats.tts_text: Hi, I'm Vuh-roon Nigh-yar. I volunteer on the Medhavy project at Humanitarians AI. This video covers my second month, June twenty twenty-six: standing up a rendering toolchain from nothing, building two physics animation scenes, and being approved to continue. One hundred hours documented.

beats.narration_text: The first week produced no visible deliverable, and that is worth stating accurately. Standing up a rendering toolchain on Windows Subsystem for Linux means system libraries, a package manager that resolves paths correctly, and a filesystem that will not fight you. All of it has to work before a single frame exists.

show.event: eyebrow sets: SETUP — THE RENDER ENVIRONMENT
title sets in the serif beneath the terracotta rule
thesis wipes in
three bullets land as named

props.label: SETUP — THE RENDER ENVIRONMENT
props.thesis: Infrastructure hours that no deliverable shows.
bullets: physics-engine virtual environment initialised with uv.
First scene rendered and verified to .mp4.

beats.narration_text: Two failures had to be diagnosed before anything rendered. The package manager was resolving against the wrong environment, fixed with the active flag. And the Windows filesystem rejected the hardlinks the installer wanted, fixed by telling it to copy instead. Then the first scene rendered clean.

show.event: code card fades up; the two failure lines sit at the top
each fix types in beneath its failure as it is named
spark line lands: 'Then it rendered.'

props.title: environment — two diagnoses
props.code:
# path mismatch
uv pip install --active

# NTFS cross-filesystem hardlink warning
export UV_LINK_MODE=copy

# first verified render
main.py :: CreateCircle → .mp4

beats.narration_text: With the environment working, the actual animation began. Two scenes: the observable universe, and the Milky Way. Both started as naive approximations and both were rebuilt, because the first versions were geometrically wrong in ways an audience would feel even if they could not name it.

show.event: eyebrow sets: THE SCENES — PHYSICS VISUALISATION
title sets in the serif
thesis wipes in
three bullets land

props.label: THE SCENES — PHYSICS VISUALISATION
props.thesis: Rebuilt until the geometry was right.
bullets: Square star grid replaced with a polar-area-uniform distribution.
Circular arcs replaced with tilted logarithmic spiral arms.
Glowing galactic bulge and dense core star field added.

beats.narration_text: The star field is the clearest example. Scattering points uniformly in radius clusters them at the centre, because area grows with the square of the radius. The correct sampling takes the square root of a uniform draw. That one substitution is the difference between a diagram that looks plausible and one that is right.

show.event: the naive sampling line sits alone at the top of the card
the corrected line types in beneath it
the square-root term highlights terracotta as it is spoken
spark line lands: 'Area, not radius.'

props.title: star distribution — the correction
props.code:
# wrong: clusters toward the centre
r = R * u

# right: uniform by AREA
r = R * sqrt(u)          # u ~ U(0,1)

# spiral arms as VMobject, tilted
# logarithmic, not circular arcs

beats.narration_text: Then a real animation bug. In a scene cycling through SI base quantities, the static headings were vanishing after the first iteration. Not a rendering fault, and not a timing problem — a structural one. Something was clearing elements that were never meant to be cleared.

show.event: eyebrow sets: THE BUG — BASEQUANTITIES
title sets in the serif
thesis wipes in — the symptom
two bullets land: what vanished, and when

props.label: THE BUG — BASEQUANTITIES
props.thesis: Static elements cleared by a loop that should not have touched them.
bullets: "Symbol", "Dimension Symbol" and the underline faded after iteration one.
Root cause: a FadeOut call sitting inside the unit-cycling loop.

beats.narration_text: The fade-out call was inside the loop that cycled the units, so every pass cleared the headings along with the values. Moving it outside fixed it. The second change was subtler: swapping the transform so fixed phrases stay stationary while only the variable unit symbols morph between iterations.

show.event: the broken loop structure sets in mono
the FadeOut line highlights terracotta, then moves outside the loop
the transform swap types in beneath
spark line lands: 'Outside the loop.'

props.title: BaseQuantities — the fix
props.code:
# before — clears headings every pass
for unit in units:
    ...
    FadeOut(heading, underline)   ← inside

# after — headings survive the cycle
for unit in units:
    ...
FadeOut(heading, underline)       ← outside

# and: ReplacementTransform → TransformMatchingShapes
# fixed phrases hold; only unit symbols morph

beats.narration_text: On June fifteenth the completed videos went to Prof. Sridhar. He approved them and asked me to continue — in writing, and again verbally in the standing meeting. Later that month Prof. Nik directed a move to a new tool, with an instruction to build visualisations only for topics that genuinely warrant one. I submitted a scoped topic list for review rather than deciding alone.

show.event: eyebrow sets: APPROVAL & DIRECTION
title sets in the serif
thesis wipes in
three bullets land: approval, the tool change, the scoped list

props.label: APPROVAL & DIRECTION
props.thesis: Approved to continue — then scoped, collaboratively.
bullets: Prof. Sridhar approved the completed videos and asked for continuation.
Prof. Nik directed adoption of a new production tool.
Topic list compiled and submitted for review before building.

beats.narration_text: Videos were produced on the new tool against that approved list. The narration layer was the one piece that did not land: the API key provided for voice was disabled. Not a configuration error and not a usage limit — an inactive credential, resolvable only by whoever administers the account.

props.label: Narration credential
props.resolution: An inactive key, not a usage error. Diagnosed and reported rather than worked around.

beats.narration_text: Month two, then. A rendering toolchain stood up from nothing on an awkward platform. Two physics scenes rebuilt until the geometry was correct. A real animation bug traced to its structural cause and fixed. Professor approval to continue, in writing. And production scoped collaboratively rather than unilaterally.
